title: Secagem química de pequenos artrópodes
author: Ana Dal Molin
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.s9aeh2e

steps.title: Select Chemical Drying Agent
steps.instruction: Choose between HMDS, amyl acetate, or isoamyl acetate based on availability. If using acetate, ensure final containers are made of glass, porcelain, or resistant plastic (e.g., HDPE #2).

steps.title: Dehydrate Specimens in Ethanol
steps.instruction: Dehydrate the specimen using successive ethanol baths of increasing concentrations until reaching 100% ethanol. If the specimen is currently in 70% alcohol (malaise), start at 70%.

substeps.instruction: Replace alcohol in the container using a pipette rather than transferring the specimen.
Note: 30-minute intervals are typically sufficient for specimens smaller than 2mm.

steps.title: Ensure Complete Dehydration
steps.instruction: Leave the specimen in a second bath of 100% ethanol for at least 1 hour to guarantee complete dehydration.

steps.title: Chemical Drying Process
steps.instruction: Perform the following steps in an appropriate container; line with a small piece of filter paper if there is a risk of residue or grease causing specimens to stick.

substeps.instruction: Incubate for 1 hour in a 1:1 mixture of 100% ethanol and the chosen agent (acetate or HMDS).
Incubate for 1-2 hours in pure acetate or HMDS.
Perform a final bath of acetate or HMDS until the liquid evaporates.
Optional: Cover samples with a Petri dish during the evaporation stage for protection.
Perform evaporation inside a fume hood, especially when using HMDS, due to disruptive odors.
